parts:
You've possibly failed to receive an answer because (1) the data you
provide didn't work (on my end there were extra newlines created that
I had to manually remove), and (2) You haven't explained what you want
or how the code fails to give you what you expect.

That said, when I get your code working it does indeed look like
something funky happens with geom_area (see attached). However, take a
look at what happens if you reduce the data set:

m <- ggplot(real.media.test[real.media.test$variable %in%
levels(real.media.test$variable)[1:2],],aes(x=date,y=value,fill=variable))
m+geom_area(position='stack')+facet_wrap(~region,scales="free")

five levels of $variable. However, when we try a 6 variable area stack
(and no matter which 6), we get the odd results. Looks like a bug.

On the other hand, I actually fail to see the utility of the graph
you're requesting. The geom_line() version you cite as working looks
beautiful & very understandable whereas even looking at 2 variables in
a stacked geom_area() plot I completely lose the relationships. Then
again, maybe this is a specialized graph that is well understood in
your field?

By the way, you shouldn't email the list *and* Hadley at the same
time. Hadley checks this list so he'll get the message and doesn't
need to be double-hit.
